Seeded 3 user-A blocks + 1 user-B block via direct mongo, verified newest-first ordering, reason_label population, no _id leak, and user-A receives 404 when guessing user-B's block id. Full regression: 39/39 (12 new + 11 safety_guardian + 3 max_concurrent_race + 11 iter26_max_concurrent_endpoints + 2 iter18_diagnostic). FRONTEND: nav-safety-blocks sidebar link works, /safety-blocks route loads, goldilocks banner / sparkline / thresholds-collapsible / reason-bar / empty-state table all render. CRITICAL FRONTEND BUG FOUND: the days selector (sb-days-select) and refresh button (sb-refresh) are completely missing from the DOM because SafetyBlocks.jsx passes props `eyebrow`, `description`, `actions` to PageHeader, but PageHeader (components/AppLayout.jsx line 28) only accepts `title`, `subtitle`, `action`, `testid`. The `actions` (plural) prop is silently dropped, so users have no way to change the time window (1d/7d/30d) or refresh data — two of the six required features in the review request. The `description` and `eyebrow` text are also silently dropped.

ui_bugs.issue: Days selector (data-testid='sb-days-select') and Refresh button (data-testid='sb-refresh') are NOT rendered on /safety-blocks. PageHeader component signature is `({ title, subtitle, action, testid })` (single `action`, named `subtitle`), but SafetyBlocks.jsx passes `eyebrow`, `description`, `actions` (plural). React silently drops unrecognized props, so the actions panel and description never appear in the DOM. Empty-state page works because everything else lives inside `children`, not header props.

integration_issues.issue: Cannot be exercised from the UI — the <select> is never mounted. Backend supports days=1..90 correctly (tests pass), but the user has no way to invoke it. Refresh button likewise missing.

issues: Missing eyebrow ('Safety / risk envelope') and description ('Trades the guardian refused before they could reach the broker.') because PageHeader does not accept those prop names. Visually the header is bare — just the 'Safety Blocks' H1.

action_items: Fix /app/frontend/src/pages/SafetyBlocks.jsx PageHeader call: rename `description` → `subtitle`, `actions` → `action`, drop `eyebrow` (unsupported) OR extend PageHeader in components/AppLayout.jsx to accept `eyebrow`/`description`/`actions` aliases. Easiest fix: change line ~212-232 of SafetyBlocks.jsx to use `subtitle={...}` and `action={...}`.

After fix, re-verify: data-testid='sb-days-select' visible, can change to 30, triggers GET /api/safety-blocks/stats?days=30; data-testid='sb-refresh' visible, click triggers re-fetch; description text 'Trades the guardian refused before they could reach the broker.' is visible under the H1.
critical_code_review_comments: PageHeader prop mismatch (above) is the only blocker.

safety_blocks_routes.py uses ISO string for blocked_at and Python-side bucketing for by_day. Works, but lexicographic compare on ISO strings is correct only because UTC ISO is monotonic; if blocked_at is ever stored with mixed offsets (e.g. naive local), the $gte cutoff filter will silently miss rows. Consider storing as BSON datetime + using $dateTrunc for native aggregation.

_serialize() does `audit: doc.get('audit')` and `context: doc.get('context')` — both can be arbitrary nested dicts containing future ObjectIds. Today the seed data uses plain dicts so it works, but if execution.py ever stores an `_id` inside context (e.g. position_id from positions collection), the response will fail JSON encoding. Defensive: run a deep-strip-ObjectId pass on audit/context.

Stats endpoint hard-caps the by_day projection at length=10000 — fine for days<=90 with normal usage, but a noisy account could overflow this on days=90. Either use aggregation pipeline ($group on date) or paginate.

REASON_LABELS in safety_blocks_routes.py and the audit-name strings in safety_guardian.py are maintained in two places. Add a shared enum or import REASON_LABELS from safety_guardian to prevent drift (already saw 'risk_inputs_present' added since iter18).

SafetyBlocks.jsx renders threshold values as `{v}%` for every value — but `get_guardian_config()` returns thresholds in mixed units (some are %, some may be raw counts in future like max_concurrent_cap). Will display nonsensical '5%' for a max_concurrent integer if such a field is added.

BlockRow expanded state is keyed by block.id (string OK), but expanding a row only shows ACCOUNT STATE + AUDIT TRAIL; for a refused-trade postmortem it would help to also show entry/sl/tp from the original signal context. Currently those are not in `context` so the user can't reproduce why the guardian rejected.
